tldr: Voice agents hear everyone near the phone, so we built Nearfield, an open-source model that keeps the caller's voice and cuts the rest.
what: This piece is about voice agents answering the wrong voice. On a real call the microphone picks up a TV, a café, or a second person, and noise suppression keeps those voices because they are speech too. Nearfield adds a small head to DeepFilterNet3 that sorts near voice from background.
why: An agent that hears every voice replies to the wrong person or cuts itself off when the TV starts a new sentence. Clean audio is not enough. The agent needs the caller's audio alone, or the caller repeats themselves and asks for a human.
how: DeepFilterNet3's internal features already encode how far and how reverberant a voice is. A 562k parameter head reads them and, every 10 ms for each of 32 bands, decides caller or background. A keep/cut rule removes the rest. On 48 held-out simulated calls the default cuts background to -41 dB at STOI 0.882, versus -16 dB alone, within 30 ms.
takeaway: The hard part was already inside a noise suppressor. A small head and a simple rule let a voice agent know who it is talking to.
